errorMonitoring.title: Error monitoring
errorMonitoring.intro: We use the error monitoring service Sentry so that we can diagnose crashes and unexpected errors, on both the website and the API. When an error occurs, the following goes to Sentry:
errorMonitoring.item1: The error itself: its message and the technical stack trace.
errorMonitoring.item2: The address of the page the error happened on, plus browser and operating system details.
errorMonitoring.item3: The IP address of your connection.
errorMonitoring.recipient: Recipient: Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.). The records are processed on Sentry's European Union (Germany) infrastructure.
errorMonitoring.legalBasis: Legal basis: legitimate interest — keeping the service secure and available, and finding and fixing faults.
errorMonitoring.limits: We deliberately keep session replay and performance tracing switched off: your screen is not recorded, your browsing behaviour is not tracked, and your form contents are not sent. Your application data, your CV and email contents are never included in an error record.
errorMonitoring.retention: Error records are deleted when Sentry's retention period expires; they are never written to the product's own database.

visitCounter.title: Visit counter
visitCounter.intro: We count how often public pages are opened, on our own server. A visit records only:
visitCounter.item1: The address of the public page opened (everything after the question mark excluded) and the page's language.
visitCounter.item2: Which site you found us from — the domain only.
visitCounter.item3: A daily counter — how many times that combination was seen that day.
visitCounter.recipient: Recipient: none. The data stays on our own server; it is sent to no analytics service and to no other third party.
visitCounter.legalBasis: No stored row can be linked to a person — no visitor id, no session id, no IP address, no browser details — so there is no personal data here. Should it be assessed otherwise, the basis is legitimate interest (KVKK art. 5/2-f, GDPR art. 6/1-f): measuring whether the service is used at all.
visitCounter.limits: No cookie is used, nothing is written to your browser, and there is no profiling or ad targeting. If your browser has “Do Not Track” switched on, nothing is counted. See “Visit counter” in the Cookie Policy for the details.
visitCounter.retention: Retention: the rows are aggregate counts holding no personal data, so they are kept indefinitely.

dataCollection.title: What data we collect and why
dataCollection.intro: e-kariyerim is a personal tool that helps you track your job applications. To provide the service, we process the following data:
dataCollection.item1: Account details: first name, last name, email address and password (stored hashed). If you sign in with Google, LinkedIn or GitHub, that account's identifier is stored instead of a password (see below).
dataCollection.item2: Application data you enter or import: company, job listing, application status, dates, and notes.
dataCollection.item3: Reminders derived from this data (follow-up suggestions, no-response alerts).
dataCollection.item4: If you turn on Gmail Scanning (an opt-in browser-extension feature), the subject line and a short snippet of a detected status-update email — used to detect a status change and, for a job not yet tracked, to read off the company/role — are stored on your account and, for that detection, sent to OpenAI. This content is first evaluated locally in your browser; only a message that looks job-application-related ever reaches us. See "Cross-border data transfer" below.
dataCollection.outro: This data is used solely to provide you with application tracking and personal analytics features.
dataCollection.item5: An HR contact you keep for an application or a job you track: name, email address and LinkedIn profile URL. You can enter these yourself; in addition, when you match a status-update email to an application and confirm it, that email's sender address may be filled in as the HR email — automated mailboxes (no-reply and the like) and job-platform addresses are never stored for this, and an address filled this way is labelled "from an incoming email" in the interface. Only you can see it; it is never shown to other users, never included in any analytics, never sent anywhere, and it is deleted along with the application or your account. We never email that address on our own — in the interface it is only a link.

googleSignIn.title: Sign in with Google
googleSignIn.intro: Sign in with Google is an optional login method, an alternative to registering with email and password. When you use it, we receive only the following from Google:
googleSignIn.item1: Your Google account's permanent identifier (so we can recognise your account even if your email address changes).
googleSignIn.item2: Your email address, as verified by Google.
googleSignIn.item3: The first and last name on your Google profile (pre-filled in the sign-up form; you can change them before saving).
googleSignIn.noAccess: We do not access, and never request permission for, your Gmail, contacts, Drive or any other data in your Google account. We do not store the access tokens Google issues us; they are discarded as soon as sign-in completes.
googleSignIn.linking: If the verified email address of your Google account already belongs to an e-kariyerim account created with a password, the Google sign-in is linked to that account and signs you into it; your password keeps working.
googleSignIn.revoke: You can remove the permission on Google's side at any time under Google Account → Security → Third-party apps. Deleting your e-kariyerim account also removes the link to Google.

linkedInSignIn.title: Sign in with LinkedIn
linkedInSignIn.intro: Sign in with LinkedIn is an optional login method, an alternative to registering with email and password. When you use it, we receive only the following from LinkedIn:
linkedInSignIn.item1: Your LinkedIn account's permanent identifier (so we can recognise your account even if your email address changes).
linkedInSignIn.item2: Your email address, as verified by LinkedIn — if LinkedIn shares it. LinkedIn does not always do so; in that case we ask you to enter an email address yourself when you complete your sign-up, and that address is not verified by us.
linkedInSignIn.item3: The first and last name on your LinkedIn profile (pre-filled in the sign-up form; you can change them before saving).
linkedInSignIn.noAccess: We do not access, and never request permission for, your connections, messages, posts or any other data in your LinkedIn account. We do not store the access tokens LinkedIn issues us; they are discarded as soon as sign-in completes.
linkedInSignIn.linking: If the email address verified by LinkedIn already belongs to an e-kariyerim account created with a password, the LinkedIn sign-in is linked to that account and signs you into it; your password keeps working. An email address you typed in yourself is never used to link to an existing account.
linkedInSignIn.revoke: You can remove the permission on LinkedIn's side at any time under Settings & Privacy → Data privacy → Other applications → Permitted services. Deleting your e-kariyerim account also removes the link to LinkedIn.

gitHubSignIn.title: Sign in with GitHub
gitHubSignIn.intro: Sign in with GitHub is an optional login method, an alternative to registering with email and password. When you use it, we receive only the following from GitHub:
gitHubSignIn.item1: Your GitHub account's numeric identifier (so we can recognise your account even if you change your username or email address).
gitHubSignIn.item2: Your email address, as verified by GitHub — if GitHub shares one. An account that keeps its address private shares none; in that case we ask you to enter an email address yourself when you complete your sign-up, and that address is not verified by us.
gitHubSignIn.item3: The display name on your GitHub profile, split into a first and last name (pre-filled in the sign-up form; you can change them before saving).
gitHubSignIn.noAccess: We ask GitHub for two permissions only — read your profile and read your email addresses. We do not access, and never request permission for, your repositories (public or private), your code, your issues or anything else in your GitHub account. We do not store the access tokens GitHub issues us; they are discarded as soon as sign-in completes.
gitHubSignIn.linking: If the email address verified by GitHub already belongs to an e-kariyerim account created with a password, the GitHub sign-in is linked to that account and signs you into it; your password keeps working. An email address you typed in yourself is never used to link to an existing account.
gitHubSignIn.revoke: You can remove the permission on GitHub's side at any time under Settings → Applications → Authorized OAuth Apps. Deleting your e-kariyerim account also removes the link to GitHub.

crossBorderTransfer.title: Cross-border data transfer
crossBorderTransfer.intro: Your data goes abroad in two cases. The first is Gmail Scanning: if you turn it on, the subject line and a short summary of each detected status-update email are sent abroad to work out what it means for your application.
crossBorderTransfer.recipient: Recipient: OpenAI, L.L.C. (United States) — our API provider.
crossBorderTransfer.purpose: Purpose: to classify the email's application-status signal, and — for a job not yet tracked — to read off a company name and job title; this only runs when a simpler, local rule-based check doesn't already recognize the email.
crossBorderTransfer.legalBasis: Legal basis: this only happens for Gmail Scanning you turn on yourself in the browser extension; nothing is sent unless you use this feature.
crossBorderTransfer.withdraw: Withdrawal: turn off Gmail Scanning in the browser extension's Settings page. Or delete your account, to stop this entirely.
crossBorderTransfer.sensitiveDataNote: The subject and snippet are also stored on your account (visible to you when reviewing a suggestion) — never the full email body.
crossBorderTransfer.feedbackTransfer: The second is feedback: when you send feedback from inside the app, your message and its technical context are copied to a private repository on GitHub so it can be tracked. Recipient: GitHub, Inc. (Microsoft, United States). Your name, your account email address and your reply address are not sent. Lawful basis: legitimate interest — tracking and fixing what users report. See the "Feedback you send" section above for the detail.

cvStorage.title: CVs you upload
cvStorage.intro: Uploading a CV is entirely optional; the rest of the service works without one. When you do upload a CV:
cvStorage.where: The file is stored in a bucket closed to the public on Google Cloud in the European Union region (europe-west1) — the same region as your account and application data. Even a guessed address cannot reach it; the bucket is not exposed to the internet at all.
cvStorage.access: Only you, while signed in, can reach the file. Every download is checked against your own account and streamed through the e-kariyerim server; no shareable or time-limited link is ever produced. It is never shown to other users, to employers or to job boards.
cvStorage.noTransfer: The contents of your CV are never sent to any third party, AI services included. The file is not read, converted to text or analysed; it is only stored and handed back to you. The first-page preview you see on the My CVs page is rendered in your own browser, not on the server.
cvStorage.deletion: A CV you delete is deleted permanently — the storage-side recovery window is deliberately turned off. Deleting your account deletes all of your CVs with it.
cvStorage.sensitiveDataNote: A CV can carry more than your work history — a photo, a date of birth, or health or military-service information — which is why we ask for your explicit consent before each upload. What goes into it is your decision: none of those fields are needed for the service to work, and you can delete the file at any time.
cvStorage.consent: The lawful basis is your explicit consent, and it is taken separately for every upload: you tick the consent box before choosing a file, the box is never pre-ticked, and it clears again after each upload. You can withdraw consent at any time by deleting the file, and deleting your account deletes all of your CVs with it.

cvScan.title: CV scan (without signing in)
cvScan.intro: On the public CV scan page you can upload a PDF or Word file and see what an applicant tracking system reads from it. This is separate from, and different to, "CVs you upload" above:
cvScan.noStorage: The file is not stored anywhere. It is never written to disk on the server and never placed in storage; it exists in memory for the length of the request and is gone once the response is sent. The text of your CV is not kept either.
cvScan.retained: Three things survive a scan: your IP address, to enforce the scan limit (deleted after 2 hours), an anonymous score (a number from 0 to 100, with no record of which file it came from or whose it was), and a scan counter.
cvScan.noTransfer: The contents of your CV are not sent to any third party — AI services included. The score is produced entirely by fixed-rule checks running on our own server; no language model is involved.
cvScan.output: The excerpts and the raw text you see on the result screen exist only inside the response to your own request; they are not recorded and never written to logs.
cvScan.consent: The legal basis is your explicit consent, taken separately for every scan: the consent box is never pre-ticked and is cleared again after each scan. Since nothing is stored, there is no retention to withdraw — not running the scan is enough.

feedback.title: Feedback you send
feedback.intro: The feedback button in the bottom-right corner of every page is entirely optional. When you send a message:
feedback.what: Your message, the topic you picked (bug/idea/question) and, if you chose one, how you said it was going are stored against your account.
feedback.context: Technical context is stored with it: the path of the page you opened the panel from (for example /en/applications), your language and theme, and your browser details. Only the path of the address is taken — query parameters (an application id, say) are dropped both in your browser and on the server.
feedback.notCollected: The contents of your applications, CVs and emails are not sent with feedback, and no screenshot is taken.
feedback.replyEmail: The reply address is optional and can be left blank; it is used only to get back to you, never for marketing.
feedback.deletion: Deleting your account deletes your feedback from our database. The tracking record on GitHub never carried your identity, so after that deletion it can no longer be traced back to you; if you would like that record removed as well, just write to us.
feedback.legalBasis: Lawful basis: legitimate interest — fixing and improving the product against what users report.
feedback.mirror: Your message and the technical context above are also opened as a tracking record in a private repository on GitHub, so we can follow it through. Your name, your account email address and your reply address are not sent there — only the record's id goes, so seeing who wrote it means looking it up in our own database.
feedback.mirrorRecipient: Recipient: GitHub, Inc. (Microsoft, United States). This is a transfer abroad; see the "Transfers abroad" section below.
feedback.storage: Feedback is stored in our own database; the canonical record is ours.

scope.title: What this policy covers
scope.body: This page describes the e-kariyerim Browser Extension ("the extension") only. The extension is a companion to the e-kariyerim web application (ekariyerim.com): it lets a signed-in user save a job posting they are viewing on LinkedIn or kariyer.net as a tracked application in their own account, and offers an opt-in "Gmail Scanning" feature that checks an email you open in Gmail on your own device and only sends a short summary when it looks job-related. Data already saved to your account (your past applications) is governed by e-kariyerim's own privacy policy, not this document.

access.title: What the extension accesses, and when
access.intro: The extension does nothing until you click its toolbar icon. When you do, and only if the active tab is a supported LinkedIn or kariyer.net job posting, it reads:
access.item1: The job title, company name, and location visible on that page.
access.item2: The job description text and a formatted (bold/headings/lists) snapshot of it, visible on that page.
access.item3: The page's URL, to identify the job and detect duplicates.
access.item4: On a LinkedIn posting that publicly shows a hiring-team card: the name and public profile URL of the person who posted the job, offered as the contact for that application — so you know who to follow up with. Most postings don't show one (it is the poster's own choice), and nothing is filled in when they don't.
access.outro: Every field is shown to you, editable, in the extension's popup before anything is sent anywhere — including the contact, which you can change or clear before saving.

gmail.title: Gmail Scanning (opt-in, beta)
gmail.intro: Gmail Scanning turns status-update emails (interview invites, rejections, status updates) into suggestions without ever relaying your inbox anywhere. It is off by default. You turn it on yourself, per device, from the extension's Settings page.
gmail.whileOff: While off, nothing changes: the extension reads nothing on mail.google.com.
gmail.whenOn: Once turned on, whenever you personally open an email in Gmail, the extension reads that one message — sender address, subject line, and body text (capped at 2000 characters) — directly from the page, in your own browser. It never reads your inbox list, and never reads a message you haven't opened.
gmail.localScoring: That text is scored entirely on your device, against a small table of job-application-related keywords and known job-site/ATS domains, downloaded from e-kariyerim and cached locally. This table contains no personal data, only generic vocabulary and domain names.
gmail.whatIsSent: Only if that on-device score suggests the email is genuinely job-application-related does the extension send anything: the sender address, subject line, and the same capped snippet — never the full email body, and never anything about a message that didn't score as relevant — to your own e-kariyerim account, to be turned into a suggestion you can review. An email that scores as unrelated (which is most email — personal messages, receipts, newsletters, and so on) is never sent anywhere and is discarded the moment scoring finishes.
gmail.dedupe: The extension also keeps a small local list (on your device) of email threads it has already submitted, so re-opening the same email doesn't send a duplicate. This list, and the keyword table above, never leave your device except as the read-only fetch that downloads the table.

stored.title: What the extension stores
stored.intro: The extension stores the following locally on your device, using the browser's own chrome.storage.local (never Chrome Sync, never a third-party server):
stored.item1: The e-kariyerim API address you're using (a setting, not personal data).
stored.item2: The access token your e-kariyerim account issued to this extension, and the date it expires (so the extension can warn you before the connection lapses instead of simply stopping). It authenticates the extension's requests as you and reaches only the endpoints the extension uses — it cannot export your application history or manage your account. You obtain it by pressing "Connect" and confirming a code on your own account page; if you use a custom API address you can still generate one in e-kariyerim's Settings and enter it by hand.
stored.item3: Your light/dark theme preference for the extension's own popup.
stored.item4: Your language choice (Turkish/English) for the extension's pages.
stored.item5: Whether you've turned on Gmail Scanning (off unless you explicitly enable it), a cached copy of the (non-personal) keyword/domain table it scores against, and a short list of email thread IDs already submitted, so the same email isn't sent twice.
stored.outro: This data never leaves your device except as described in "What the extension sends, and to whom" below.

sent.title: What the extension sends, and to whom
sent.body: When you click "I Applied," the extension sends the job title, company, location, job URL, description and contact details shown in the popup to the e-kariyerim API, authenticated with your personal access token, so it can be saved to your own e-kariyerim account. Company-name autocomplete similarly queries the e-kariyerim API with the text you've typed.
sent.hrNote: A contact saved this way is your own note of who to approach about that application: only you can see it, it is never shown to other users or included in any analytics, e-kariyerim never emails or messages that person on your behalf, and it is deleted along with the application or your account.
sent.gmailNote: If you've turned on Gmail Scanning, an opened email that scores as job-related sends its sender, subject, and a capped snippet to your own e-kariyerim account (see the Gmail Scanning section above) — this only happens for emails you open, only after you enable the setting, and only when the on-device score qualifies.
sent.noOther: The extension sends data to no other destination. It does not use analytics, advertising, or tracking services, and it does not sell or share your data with third parties.
sent.pairing: When you press "Connect," the extension asks the e-kariyerim API for a pairing code and opens the confirmation page in a tab; while it waits it asks, every few seconds, whether you have confirmed that code. Neither request carries any personal data — the extension has no account and no credential at that point. The only thing that comes back is the access token, once, after you confirm. If you refuse on that page, or the code runs out of time, nothing is issued at all.

controls.title: Your controls
controls.item1: The job-tracking popup only acts when you click its icon — there is no background scraping or polling on LinkedIn/kariyer.net.
controls.item2: Gmail Scanning is off by default and does nothing until you turn it on in Settings; once on, it only reads an email when you personally open it in Gmail — it does not scan your inbox in the background, and does nothing at all on any other site. Turn it off anytime in Settings, with the same immediate effect.
controls.item3: You can remove your access token at any time from the extension's Settings page, or revoke it from e-kariyerim's Settings → Browser Extension page, which invalidates it immediately. It also expires on its own after 90 days, whether or not you do anything.
controls.item4: Uninstalling the extension deletes everything chrome.storage.local held for it (the token, API address, theme, language preference, Gmail Scanning setting, and its local caches) from your device.
controls.item5: A pairing code is only ever an offer: it grants nothing until you confirm it while signed in, and the confirmation page has a "this wasn't me" button for a code you did not produce yourself.

appPolicy.before: Everything the extension sends goes to your own e-kariyerim account. How that data is stored, how long it is kept, and what rights you have over it are described in the

intro.title: In short
intro.body: e-kariyerim uses exactly two cookies, both needed for the service to work. We use no advertising cookies, no tracking pixels, no analytics tool such as Google Analytics, and no third-party cookies at all. That is why you never see a cookie consent banner here: there is no optional cookie to leave to your choice.
intro.legalNote: Under Turkish data protection law (KVKK), strictly necessary and functional cookies do not require explicit consent — what they require is disclosure. This page is that disclosure.

table.title: The cookies we use
table.name: Name
table.localePurpose: Remembers which language a page opens in (Turkish/English). Our server writes it to match the language in the address bar, and updates it when you switch languages.
table.localeDuration: Session: deleted when you close the browser
table.themePurpose: Remembers your light/dark theme preference. Written only when you press the theme button, or when you sign in and the preference stored on your account is applied.
table.note: Both store nothing but a preference: neither contains an identifier, a user number or a tracking code, and neither is sent to any third party.

storage.title: Browser storage (localStorage and sessionStorage)
storage.intro: These are not cookies, but they store data on your device in the same way, so we list them here too:
storage.item1: Session tokens — aa_access_token, aa_refresh_token, their expiry times, and aa_user (your name, email address and interface preferences). They keep you signed in; they live in localStorage and are deleted when you sign out.
storage.item2: Sign-in security keys — aa_google_oauth, aa_linkedin_oauth and aa_github_oauth. These are single-use values that block a CSRF attack during a Google, LinkedIn or GitHub sign-in; they live in sessionStorage and are deleted the moment the sign-in completes.
storage.outro: Both are required for the service to work — without them you cannot sign in.

visitCounter.title: Visit counter
visitCounter.intro: We count how often the site's public pages are opened, on our own server. No cookie is used, nothing is written to your browser, and nothing is sent to any third party. A visit adds only these three things to a counter:
visitCounter.item1: The address of the page opened — public pages only. Everything after the question mark (a search term, the key in a password-reset link) is cut off before it leaves your browser.
visitCounter.item2: The page's language — Turkish or English.
visitCounter.item3: Which site you found us from — the domain only (“google.com”, say), never the address on that site or the words you searched for.
visitCounter.note: None of this identifies you: no visitor id, no session id, no IP address and no browser details are stored. Two visits by the same person and one visit each by two people are therefore the same number to us, and a row can be linked neither to an account nor to another row. Even when you are signed in, this request carries none of your account's credentials.
visitCounter.noCookie: Because no cookie is written, the consent screen promised in “If this policy changes” below is not triggered here — that promise covers optional cookies. We are describing the counter anyway, so you can read what it holds.
visitCounter.dnt: If your browser has “Do Not Track” switched on, nothing is counted at all.
visitCounter.why: Why we count: there is no other way for us to see whether anyone arrives, which article is useful, or whether people who try to sign up get stuck. Counter rows are aggregate and hold no personal data, so they are kept indefinitely.

noThirdParty.title: Third parties and tracking
noThirdParty.intro: None of the following exist on this site:
noThirdParty.item1: Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, Hotjar or any comparable analytics/tracking tool.
noThirdParty.item3: Embedded third-party content (YouTube, Google Maps and the like) — we use none, so no cookies arrive behind them either.
noThirdParty.item4: Externally loaded fonts or scripts: fonts are bundled into our own server at build time, so your browser never calls Google Fonts.
noThirdParty.outro: The site's Content-Security-Policy only lets your browser connect to our own server, our own API and the error monitoring service; that list cannot grow quietly.

errorMonitoring.title: Error monitoring
errorMonitoring.before: We use Sentry so that we can diagnose unexpected errors. Sentry writes no cookie and stores nothing in your browser, but it does create a record when an error occurs. What is sent, where it goes and which legal basis it rests on is set out in detail in
errorMonitoring.link: the error monitoring section of the Privacy Policy
errorMonitoring.after: . Session replay and performance tracing are switched off; your browsing behaviour is not tracked.

control.title: How to remove cookies
control.body: You can delete this site's cookies and site data from your browser's settings at any time, and you can block cookies entirely. The effect: your language and theme preferences fall back to the defaults, and if you also delete the session tokens you are signed out and have to sign in again. Nothing else about the site stops working.
control.accountNote: Deleting the data held in your account is a separate matter — you can do that by deleting your account from the Settings page.

changes.title: If this policy changes
changes.body: If we ever add an optional cookie for analytics, advertising or anything similar, we will update this page before adding it and turn on a consent screen where each category can be chosen separately and everything defaults to off. No such cookie will be written without your consent.

This page walks through everything from creating your account to logging an application with one click from the Chrome extension.

gettingStarted.title: Signing Up and Logging In
gettingStarted.intro: Getting started with e-kariyerim only takes a few details — no credit card, no waiting on a confirmation email.

step1.title: Enter your first and last name
step1.body: Used to identify you throughout the app (e.g. the name shown on the dashboard and in the NavBar).

step3.title: Accept the Privacy Policy
step3.body: The account can't be created without checking the consent box under the sign-up form.

step4.title: Submit
step4.body: You're taken straight to the Dashboard — no email verification to wait for.

login.title: Log in
login.body: Log in with the email and password you registered with. On login, your last saved theme (light/dark) and language preference are applied automatically.

calloutTheme.title: Your dark-mode preference carries over at sign-up
calloutTheme.body: If you switched to dark mode in your browser before signing up, your new account opens in dark mode too — new accounts otherwise start in light mode.

dashboard.title: What's on the Dashboard?
dashboard.intro: The Dashboard you land on after logging in summarizes your whole application process on one screen. The one-line summary under the heading gives you the three numbers that matter most, and the "New Application" button in the top right lets you add a new application directly.

hero.title: Open applications and the weekly trend
hero.body: The largest figure on the page is the total still waiting for a reply. The small chart beneath it shows how many applications you sent per week over the last 12 weeks. The four tiles beside it give your interview, offer, rejection and ghosting counts, each with its share of the total.

funnel.title: Conversion funnel
funnel.body: Shows how much of each stage made it to the next one along applied → replied → interview → offer. When the raw numbers are far apart (thousands of applications, a handful of interviews), every rail is still drawn at its own full width, so the small stages stay readable. The line underneath names the stage with the steepest drop-off.

responseTime.title: Response time
responseTime.body: The median and average number of days from applying to first response, together with how many replied applications they were computed from. If the average sits well above the median, a note says so — a few very late replies pull it up. If nothing has been answered yet, an empty state is shown instead.

breakdown.title: Status breakdown
breakdown.body: Horizontal bars showing which status your applications are in. If one status is crowded enough to flatten the rest (usually "Applied" after a bulk import), it is drawn full-width on its own scale, and the remaining records are listed below it on a scale of their own.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.body: A breakdown of applications that have finished: offer/accepted, no answer, withdrawn and rejected. The band at the top shows their proportions and the line at the bottom gives your win rate. Applications still in flight are left out of this.

trackedJobs.title: Note jobs you haven't applied to yet
trackedJobs.intro: Tracked Jobs is a lightweight watchlist for jobs you're interested in but haven't applied to yet. Unlike an Application, it has no status, timeline, or employment type — just company, title, location, job URL, and your notes.

step2.title: Enter the company name and job title
step2.body: Optionally add the location, job URL, and your own notes.

step3.title: Save it
step3.body: The job appears in your list with the date it was added.

step1.title: Click "Mark as Applied" next to the job
step1.body: This opens a small inline form.

step2.title: Enter the employment type and applied date
step2.body: You can add extra notes too.

step3.title: Confirm
step3.body: The job is removed from your tracked list and created as a real Application — you're taken straight to its detail page.

remove.title: Remove a job
remove.body: If you're no longer interested, "Remove" deletes it from the list permanently.

calloutNoEdit.title: There's no direct edit
calloutNoEdit.body: There's currently no way to edit a tracked job's details. If something's wrong, remove it and re-add it; if you've already applied, converting it with "Mark as Applied" and then editing the resulting Application is the way to fix the details.

applications.title: Create, track, edit, and delete your applications
applications.intro: Applications are the heart of e-kariyerim: each one has its own status, timeline, and (if available) job description.

step1.title: Click "New Application" from the Dashboard or Applications page

step2.title: Start typing the company name
step2.body: Companies you've added before are suggested as autocomplete; for a new company, just type it as-is.

step3.title: Enter the job title, job URL, location, and employment type
step3.body: The applied date defaults to today, but you can change it.

step4.title: Optionally add a source, a CV and notes, then save
step4.body: The source field can only be chosen when creating — it can't be changed later. If you have files on the My CVs page you can record which one you applied with; your default CV arrives already selected.

list.title: List, search, filter
list.body: The Applications list is paginated (10 per page) and supports searching by company/title, filtering by status, and sorting by date/company/title/status — all your filters are reflected in the URL, so you can share or bookmark a view.

detail.title: Application detail
detail.body: Opening an application shows its status badge, location, employment type, applied date, when it was added, the job URL (if any), the CV you recorded it with and your notes, with the Timeline and — if available — the job description below. Applications created automatically via Gmail Scanning show a "Created from Email" badge.

contact.title: HR contact and company links
contact.body: Under "Contact", an application can hold the person to follow up with — name, email address and LinkedIn profile. You can type them in yourself; the extension fills them in from the hiring-team card when a LinkedIn posting shows one, and confirming an email suggestion adds the sender's address the same way. Beside it the company's own website, LinkedIn and kariyer.net pages appear, along with its industry and country once they can be worked out. All of it is yours alone to see — e-kariyerim never writes to that person on your behalf.

edit.title: Editing
edit.body: "Edit" on the detail page lets you update the job title, job URL, location, employment type, applied date, and notes. The company name and source can't be changed after creation.

delete.title: Deleting
delete.body: Clicking "Delete" on the detail page opens a confirmation dialog — nothing is deleted until you confirm. To clear out several at once, select them on the list instead (see "Acting on many applications at once").

calloutConfirm.title: Deletion can't be undone
calloutConfirm.body: Deleting an application permanently removes its entire history, including its timeline.

step1.title: Click "Change Status" on the detail page

step2.title: Pick the new status from the list
step2.body: Your current status doesn't appear in the list — only the statuses you can move to.

step3.title: Optionally add a note and confirm
step3.body: The change is recorded in the Status History section as "Old Status → New Status", together with your note, which appears under that row.

statuses.title: What do the statuses mean?
statuses.body: An application can be in one of these statuses: Applied, Screening, Interview, TechnicalInterview, FinalInterview, Offer, Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Ghosted.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.body: The detail page gathers everything that happened to an application into one chronological list, newest first: every status change and every event you added yourself. A status row says which status it moved from and to, when, the note you wrote at the time, and — most importantly — how the change was applied: whether you changed it yourself, confirmed an email suggestion, changed it as part of a bulk action, or undid one. For a change that came from an email, the rejection reason and the originating email's subject can be expanded inline.

addEvent.title: Adding an event yourself
addEvent.body: Not everything worth remembering is a status change. "Add event" records things like a recruiter getting in touch, a screening starting, an interview being scheduled or completed, an offer arriving, or a follow-up you sent — with the date it happened and a short note. Leave the date empty and it is recorded as now. The event joins the same timeline without moving the application's status.

companyView.title: Grouping by company
companyView.body: The List / Company switch above the list collects the same applications under the company you sent them to. In the company view a page holds 10 companies rather than 10 applications — so a company's applications are never split across two pages. Each company header shows how many applications you have there, how they are spread across statuses, and when something last moved; click the header to fold a group away, or use its checkbox to select all of that company's applications at once. Search and the status filter work the same way in both views, and the view you pick is reflected in the URL. If you have more than 20 applications at one company, the link under the group takes you to the flat list narrowed to it.

bulk.title: Acting on many applications at once
bulk.body: Tick the box on any row and an action bar appears at the bottom of the screen with two things you can do to the selection: change the status of all of it, or delete all of it. The box in the table header takes the whole page, and next to the count there is a link that reaches past it — every application the current search and filters match, not just the ten in front of you.

step1.title: Select the rows
step1.body: Row by row, a whole page at a time, or everything matching the filter. In the company view, the box on a group header takes that company's listed applications.

step2.title: Pick an action from the bar
step2.body: "Change status" moves every selected application to one status and can carry a note. "Delete" removes them.

step3.title: Confirm
step3.body: A status change asks once and tells you how many rows will actually move — applications already in that status are counted separately and left alone. Deleting asks for more: a tick to acknowledge it, and for "all matching" also the scope spelled out and the word typed in.

undo.title: Undoing a bulk status change
undo.body: After a status change, a strip stays on the list with an "Undo" button. It puts each application back where it was — except any you have moved on yourself since, which are left alone, because a decision you made later should win. The undo is added to each application's timeline rather than erasing the change it reverses: the mistake stays on the record.

calloutDelete.title: A bulk delete cannot be undone
calloutDelete.body: There is no recycle bin. Deleted applications, their timelines and the HR contacts attached to them are gone for good; the CV files themselves stay on the My CVs page. If you are not sure, export your data from Settings first.

suggestions.title: Automatic status suggestions from your emails
suggestions.intro: Once you turn on Gmail Scanning in the browser extension (see the Chrome Extension page), the system reads status-update emails you open and offers status suggestions — so you don't have to process every update by hand.

how.title: How a suggestion appears
how.body: Once a scanned email is processed, a card appears on the Suggestions page with the company, job title, received date, a confidence percentage, and a suggested status (if any). A suggestion that doesn't match a known application yet is marked with a "New Job" badge; if no clear status could be inferred, the card shows "Still Pending" instead.

step1.title: Review the card
step1.body: Check the subject line and email snippet to make sure the suggestion is about the right application.

step2.title: "Confirm" to apply it, or "Dismiss" to skip it
step2.body: Confirm creates a new application (if it's new) or moves an existing one to the suggested status. Dismiss closes the suggestion without changing anything.

calloutConfidence.title: Check the confidence percentage
calloutConfidence.body: When confidence is low, read the email snippet first — automatic extraction isn't always exact, so you have the final say.

import.title: Bring in your LinkedIn history in bulk
import.intro: Right now the only import method is LinkedIn's own data export file (a .zip). There's no separate CSV uploader. Most of the work happens on LinkedIn's side; the steps below walk you through it end to end.

step1.title: Request your data export from LinkedIn — pick "Jobs" only
step1.body: On LinkedIn, open Settings & Privacy → Data privacy → Get a copy of your data. "Download larger data archive" takes 24 hours to prepare; choose the second option instead and tick only the "Jobs" box, and the archive usually arrives by email within 10 minutes. The "Job Applications.csv" we need for your application history is already in that selection.

step2.title: Download the .zip from the link LinkedIn emails you
step2.body: LinkedIn emails you once the archive is ready. Save the file to your computer and don't unzip it — the .zip itself is what you upload.

step3.title: Open the Import page in e-kariyerim
step3.body: Go to "Import" from the top navigation. The page walks you through the same steps visually.

step4.title: Drag the .zip into the upload area
step4.body: Drop the file onto the upload area, or click it to pick the file. As soon as it uploads, the status switches to "processing".

step5.title: Watch the progress live
step5.body: You'll see a progress bar with the number of rows processed so far; no need to leave the page.

step6.title: Review the summary
step6.body: When it finishes, you'll see how many new applications were added, how many were already there (duplicates), and how many rows couldn't be processed (invalid); any failing rows are listed individually.

calloutUnzip.title: Don't unzip the archive
calloutUnzip.body: The most common mistake is opening the zip and uploading the "Job Applications.csv" inside it on its own — that is rejected. And if you didn't tick the "Jobs" box when requesting the archive, that file isn't in the zip at all; in that case you'll need to request a fresh archive from LinkedIn.

calloutCsv.title: Only LinkedIn import is available
calloutCsv.body: There's currently no interface for uploading a hand-prepared CSV file. Applications created through import default to "FullTime" employment type, since LinkedIn's data doesn't specify one — edit the application afterwards if you need to change it.

settings.title: Account Settings
settings.intro: Settings is where you export your data, manage the browser extension's connection and delete your account. Theme and language are switched from the top menu, not from Settings.

export.title: Export My Data
export.body: Download all of your application, import, and reminder data as a single JSON file.

step1.title: Install the extension and click its icon

step2.title: Press "Connect" and confirm on the page that opens
step2.body: There is no key to copy; the extension connects the moment you confirm.

step3.title: See and revoke connections here
step3.body: The "Browser Extension" section lists each connection's name, when it was created and expires, and when it was last used. "Revoke" invalidates it immediately.

step4.title: Entering a key by hand is still there, under "advanced"
step4.body: Only needed if you point the extension at a different API address. The key is shown once, and at most 10 can be active.

calloutToken.title: The connection only reaches the endpoints the extension uses
calloutToken.body: The key given to the extension can add applications, search companies and — if you turn it on — send email signals. It cannot export your application history or manage your account. Still give it only to your own browser: it expires on its own after 90 days, and "Revoke" invalidates it immediately if you ever have doubts.

delete.title: Delete My Account
delete.body: Enter your password, type "DELETE" into the box, and click the button. A second warning tells you that all of your data will be deleted; once you confirm that too, your account and all of your data are permanently deleted.

calloutIrreversible.title: This can't be undone
calloutIrreversible.body: Once your account is deleted, all of your application, import, and reminder data is permanently gone — there's no way to reverse it.

chromeExtension.title: One-click application logging on LinkedIn and kariyer.net
chromeExtension.intro: The e-kariyerim Chrome extension turns a LinkedIn or kariyer.net job posting into a tracked application with one click — just press "I Applied".

install.title: Installation
install.storeIntro: The e-kariyerim extension is live on the Chrome Web Store — one-click install, no developer mode needed.

step1.title: Add the extension to Chrome from the link above
step1.body: Click "Add to Chrome" on the Chrome Web Store page. The extension icon appears in your toolbar.

step2.title: Click the extension icon and press "Connect"
step2.body: Sign in (or create an account) on the confirmation page that opens and confirm the code — there is no key to copy.

installManual.title: Alternative: unpacked install (developer/testing only)
installManual.intro: If you can't use the Store version — for example, you're testing an unreleased development build — you can also load the extension manually:

step1.title: Open chrome://extensions
step1.body: Just type it into the address bar and press Enter.

step2.title: Turn on "Developer mode"
step2.body: Found in the top right of the page.

step3.title: Click "Load unpacked" and select the extension folder
step3.body: The extension icon appears in your toolbar.

step1.title: Click the e-kariyerim icon in your toolbar

step2.title: Click "Connect"
step2.body: The extension produces a pairing code and opens the confirmation page in a new tab. If you are not signed in yet, you can do that there — the code is not lost.

step3.title: Check the code matches, then confirm
step3.body: The code on the page must match the one the extension is showing. Once you confirm, the extension connects within a few seconds. The connection is valid for 90 days; the extension warns you before it lapses, and renewing it is the same "Connect" button. If you point the extension at a different API address, entering a key by hand is still available under "advanced" in its settings.

step1.title: Open a LinkedIn or kariyer.net job posting page

step2.title: Click the extension icon
step2.body: It tries to auto-fill the company, title, and location from the page.

step3.title: Check the fields and correct anything that's off
step3.body: Auto-fill isn't always perfect — every field is editable before you submit.

step4.title: Click "I Applied"
step4.body: Your application is saved to e-kariyerim.

calloutScraping.title: Auto-fill is best-effort
calloutScraping.body: LinkedIn and kariyer.net occasionally change their page layout, which can leave some fields empty. That shows up as a blank field for you to fill in by hand, rather than submitting wrong data.

calloutDedupe.title: Clicking the same job again is safe
calloutDedupe.body: If you click "I Applied" again on the same job posting, it won't create a duplicate — the system finds your existing application by the job's URL and returns that instead.

q1.question: What happens if someone gets hold of my Chrome extension token?
q1.answer: That token grants full access to your account. If you suspect it's been exposed, go to Settings → Browser Extension and "Revoke" it immediately, then generate a new one.

q2.question: Can I get my data back after deleting my account?
q2.answer: No. Account deletion can't be undone; all of your application, import, and reminder data is permanently deleted.

q3.question: What if the Chrome extension reads a job's details wrong?
q3.answer: Nothing gets submitted automatically — every field is editable before you click "I Applied", the popup just gives you a starting point.

q4.question: Does Gmail Scanning read my whole inbox?
q4.answer: No. It's off by default, and once turned on it only reads an email you personally open in Gmail — never your inbox list, never a message you didn't open. The check runs on your device; only a short summary of an email that looks job-application-related is ever sent to e-kariyerim.

q5.question: Can I import a file other than my LinkedIn export (e.g. Excel/CSV)?
q5.answer: Not currently — the only import path is LinkedIn's own data export .zip file.

q6.question: Can I edit a job I'm tracking?
q6.answer: There's no direct edit for Tracked Jobs; if the details are wrong, remove it and re-add it, or if you've already applied, convert it with "Mark as Applied" and update the details on the Application edit page.

q7.question: How many Chrome extension tokens can I have?
q7.answer: Up to 10 active tokens at once. You'll need to revoke one you're not using before generating a new one.

q8.question: Why does employment type always show "Full-Time" on imported or extension-added applications?
q8.answer: Neither LinkedIn's export nor the job pages the extension reads specify an employment type, so it defaults to "FullTime" — edit the application afterwards if you need the correct type.

q9.question: Can I change or delete many applications at once?
q9.answer: Yes. Tick the rows on the Applications list — or use the "select all matching" link to reach every application the current filter matches — and the action bar at the bottom offers a status change or a delete.

q10.question: I bulk-changed the wrong applications. Can I undo it?
q10.answer: A bulk status change can be undone from the strip that stays on the list afterwards; applications you have moved on yourself since are left where they are. A bulk delete cannot be undone — which is why it asks for a tick, and for the word typed in when it covers everything matching a filter.

q11.question: Is my CV shown to employers?
q11.answer: No. Files on the My CVs page are visible only to you, are never sent to a third party or to any AI service, and are not read or analysed — recording which CV an application went out with is a note to yourself.

q12.question: I have several applications at the same company. Can I see them together?
q12.answer: Switch the View toggle above the Applications list from "List" to "Company". A page then holds companies rather than rows, so one company's applications are never split across two pages.

cv.title: Keep the CVs you apply with in one place
cv.intro: My CVs is where you store the files you apply with. You can keep up to 10, download any of them, or delete them permanently. Your files are visible only to you.

step1.title: Open the My CVs page
step1.body: Go to My CVs in the top menu. Your files are listed on the left, and the selected file is previewed on the right.

step2.title: Pick or drop a file
step2.body: Tick the consent box, then press Upload CV or drag the file onto the dashed area below the list. PDF, DOC and DOCX are accepted, up to 5 MB per file.

step3.title: Watch your quota
step3.body: The counter next to the list heading shows how many files you have used. Once you reach 10, delete one before uploading another.

preview.title: Preview
preview.body: The first page of a PDF is shown in the panel on the right. That image is produced in your own browser — no copy of it is kept on the server. DOC and DOCX files cannot be previewed in a browser; download them to read them.

default.title: Default CV
default.body: Making a file your default means it arrives pre-selected when you record a new application. The first file you upload becomes the default automatically, and deleting the default passes it to your newest remaining file. You can always change the CV used field on the application form.

remove.title: Deleting
remove.body: Delete asks for a confirmation; once you confirm, the file is removed from the list and from storage permanently and cannot be recovered. Applications you recorded that CV on are not deleted — only their reference to it is cleared.

calloutPrivacy.title: Where are your CVs stored?
calloutPrivacy.body: Your files are held in a bucket closed to the public on Google Cloud in the EU region (europe-west1). They are never sent to any third party, AI services included. Because a CV can carry sensitive data such as a photo or health information, we ask for your explicit consent before each upload; the box is never pre-ticked. You can withdraw consent by deleting the file, and deleting your account deletes your files with it.

method.title: Where does this number come from?
method.source: Entirely from what people filling in this form report about themselves. It is not mixed with the application data the product collects — one is self-reported, the other measured, and pooling them into one average would corrupt the figure.
method.median: We use the median, not the mean. Answers are anonymous, so one person can answer more than once and an extreme value can be sent deliberately; a median barely moves under either, a mean is at their mercy.
method.recency: Answers covering a short period tend to read low: applications sent recently may not have had time to be answered yet.
method.privacy: No identifier is stored — no email, no IP address, no cookie. Every field is picked from a fixed list; no free text is collected.
method.threshold: A field's median is not shown until it holds at least {minimum} answers.

cvScan.title: How does a machine read your CV?
cvScan.subtitle: Upload your PDF or Word file and see what an applicant tracking system reads from it, where it gets stuck, and what to fix. No account, and the file is never stored.

form.consentLabel: I consent to my CV being processed for this scan.
form.consentDetail: The file is never written to disk; it is dropped from memory as soon as the scan finishes. See the {privacy} for detail.

retained.ip: Your IP address, for 2 hours — only to enforce the scan limit, then deleted.

afterScan.score: A score out of 100 and how it splits across four categories — the total is the sum of the subtotals.

ats.title: What an ATS is, and is not
ats.what: An ATS (Applicant Tracking System) is the software an employer collects applications in. It turns your CV into text, splits it into fields and makes it searchable by a recruiter.
ats.myth: "ATS software auto-rejects 75% of CVs" is not true. That figure traces back to a 2012 sales brochure; in a 2025 survey around 92% of recruiters said they set no automatic rejection rules at all.
ats.truth: The real risk is not rejection, it is disappearing: if the parser cannot read your experience, your CV never comes back in a search, your dates never sort, your contact field looks empty. That is exactly what this scan measures.

limits.title: What this tool cannot do
limits.noJobMatch: It does not match you against a job ad. No keyword score — "you are a 64% fit" would be a claim we cannot measure.
limits.noAts: It does not imitate one specific ATS. We cannot know whether Workday or Taleo is behind a posting; what we measure is the readability problem all parsers share.
limits.noContent: It does not judge your content. How well you describe your experience sits outside this score.

bands.good: Your CV looks fine to a parser.
bands.fair: It is readable, but you are losing information in a few places.
bands.poor: A parser cannot read a significant part of your CV.

result.deterministic: No AI produced this number: add up the four category subtotals and you get the score, and the point costs of the findings below are the other half of the same subtraction.
result.atsNote: ATS software does not auto-reject CVs — this score does not say "you will be rejected", it says "a machine cannot read this".
result.findingsNone: None of the checks found a problem.
result.previewTitle: This is how a machine reads your CV

NoTextLayer.title: There is no readable text in the file
NoTextLayer.why: Your CV is a scanned image, or a file that carries its text as drawing. A parser cannot pull a single word out of it — not even your name reaches a search.
NoTextLayer.fix: Export straight to PDF from the program you wrote it in (Word, Google Docs, Canva). Printing and scanning it, or screenshotting it, destroys the text.

details.noText: Only {wordCount} words could be extracted from the file.
details.emptyPages: {count} pages carry no text at all.

BrokenTurkishCharacters.title: Turkish letters are being broken
BrokenTurkishCharacters.why: The font cannot name its characters, or the Turkish letters are dropped on the way out. A recruiter searching for "Yazılım Mühendisi" will not find your CV.
BrokenTurkishCharacters.fix: Export the PDF in a way that embeds fonts (Word's "Embed fonts in the file", Google Docs' "Download as PDF"), or use a common typeface.

details.stripped: The text is Turkish but contains no ı, ş, ğ, ç, ö or ü at all — the letters were flattened to ASCII on export.

MultiColumnOrTableLayout.title: Two-column or table-based layout
MultiColumnOrTableLayout.why: A person's eye separates columns; a parser does not. It reads across the line and braids the two columns together, cutting your experience away from its dates.
MultiColumnOrTableLayout.fix: Move to a single column. Bring the sidebar content (skills, contact details) into the main flow, and stop using tables as a layout tool.

details.columns: A vertical band at {position}% of the page width that no word crosses — the signature of two columns.

SectionsOrDatesUnreadable.title: Sections or dates cannot be read
SectionsOrDatesUnreadable.why: A parser looks for headings first and date ranges second. An unrecognised heading means your experience lands in no field at all; without a range there is no timeline to sort.
SectionsOrDatesUnreadable.fix: Name your sections the ordinary way: Experience, Education, Skills. Give every role a plain range like "03/2021 - present".

ContactUnreadable.title: Contact details cannot be read
ContactUnreadable.why: The record created in the system has an empty e-mail or phone field. Even a CV a person liked has no address to reply to.
ContactUnreadable.fix: Put your e-mail and phone number on the first page as ordinary text — not in a header or footer, not inside an image, not behind an icon.

details.onlyInHeaderFooter: Contact details are only in the header or footer — many parsers never look there.

LengthOutOfRange.title: Length
LengthOutOfRange.why: In a long CV the relevant experience sits far down the file; in a very short one there is nothing for a parser to extract.
LengthOutOfRange.fix: Aim for two pages. Cut older roles down to a line, and stop repeating the same information in two places.

details.longEstimated: Around {pageCount} pages (a Word file's page count can only be estimated).
details.short: Only {wordCount} words came out of the file.

InconsistentFormatting.title: Too many typefaces
InconsistentFormatting.why: Every typeface is another font program that has to carry a correct character map. More of them looks noisy and raises the chance of letters breaking.
InconsistentFormatting.fix: Stay with one typeface, two at most, and carry emphasis with weight and size instead.
